sentences.zh: 在我的第一本关于英国历史的书《好日子》（Never Had It So Good）里，我想有一张照片，拍的是哈罗德·麦克米伦坐在一列某种模型小火车上，像个

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: So in the last episode, we talked about elections when they were genuine mass participation,

sentences.en: Davey.

sentences.zh: 我想说的是，这不仅仅是视野缩小的问题。

sentences.zh: 然后德国人最终以3比2逆转取胜。

sentences.en: And that is four days before polling day.
sentences.zh: 而那正是在投票日前四天。

sentences.en: So in that campaign, Wilson had been in Paris since 64.
sentences.zh: 所以在那个竞选季里，威尔逊自64年以来一直在执政。

sentences.en: He'd had a very, very rocky time in government, had to devalue the pound, all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 他在政府任职期间经历了一段非常非常动荡的时期，不得不让英镑贬值，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: You know, great sense of sort of disappointment and frustration about his government.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们对他的政府有一种强烈的失望和挫败感。

sentences.en: And yet Heath is regarded as so dreadful, as such a poor performer, that everyone thinks Wilson is going to win really easily.
sentences.zh: 然而希思却被认为太糟糕了，表现如此拉胯，以至于大家都觉得威尔逊赢起来会易如反掌。

sentences.en: And actually Wilson does something that had not been done before.
sentences.zh: 而事实上威尔逊做了一件以前从未有人做过的事。

sentences.en: So Wilson goes on walkabouts.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔逊开始进行街头走访拉票。

sentences.en: I mean, we're very familiar with that now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们现在对此已经非常熟悉了。

sentences.en: It's a lovely summer in 1970.
sentences.zh: 1970年的夏天非常美好。

sentences.en: So he's in his kind of shirt sleeves and he walks around town centres, like shaking hands with random people.
sentences.zh: 所以他穿着衬衫袖子在市中心溜达，比如和随机遇到的人握手。

sentences.en: How do you do?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Lovely to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: I'm Howard Wilson.
sentences.zh: 我是哈罗德·威尔逊。

sentences.en: Please vote for the Labour Party.
sentences.zh: 请投票给工党。

sentences.en: And no one had done that before.
sentences.zh: 以前从来没有人这么做过。

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 基本上没有。

sentences.en: So American politicians had done it.
sentences.zh: 所以美国的政客们曾这么做过。

sentences.en: And the Queen did it on a Commonwealth tour, I think, of Australia a year or so earlier.
sentences.zh: 我想女王在差不多一年前的澳大利亚英联邦之行中也这么做过。

sentences.en: I love to think the Queen is blazing a path.
sentences.zh: 我特别喜欢设想女王正在开辟一条新路。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: The Queen is a great innovator.
sentences.zh: 女王是一位伟大的革新者。

sentences.en: I mean, Wilson and the Queen got on like house and fire, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，威尔逊和女王关系好得不得了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Wilson loved the Queen.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊很喜欢女王。

sentences.en: He was her favourite prime minister, by all accounts.
sentences.zh: 据各方说法，他曾是女王最喜欢的首相。

sentences.en: So Wilson copies the Queen.
sentences.zh: 所以威尔逊在模仿女王。

sentences.en: He basically wants to take politics out of it and run a kind of smiling presidential campaign and coast to victory against Heath.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是想把政治剥离出去，搞一种面带微笑的总统式竞选，从而轻松战胜希斯赢得大选。

sentences.en: And actually, when he loses unexpectedly, Heath won by 30 seats.
sentences.zh: 而事实上，当他意外落败时，希斯以30个议席的优势获胜了。

sentences.en: Wilson said, oh, well, it was the football, of course, that cost us.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊说，哦，好吧，当然是足球害我们输了。

sentences.en: There was a feel bad factor.
sentences.zh: 当时有一种悲观情绪。

sentences.en: I think that's nonsense.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: There was a bad set of trade figures just before the election, which is much more important.
sentences.zh: 大选前夕公布了一组糟糕的贸易数据，这要重要得多。

sentences.en: And actually, I think what those bad trade figures did was they reminded people that Wilson had not been
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为那些糟糕的贸易数据起到的作用，是提醒了人们威尔逊并不是

sentences.en: a terribly good steward of the economy and they kind of reinforced existing anxieties.
sentences.zh: 一个十分称职的经济管家，它们在某种程度上加剧了现有的焦虑。

sentences.en: And he'd let the Beatles break up.
sentences.zh: 而且他还让披头士乐队解散了。

sentences.en: So yeah, all kinds of reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，各种原因都有。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You always say that about Howard Wilson.
sentences.zh: 你总是这样评价哈罗德·威尔逊。

sentences.en: I think that's very harsh.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太严厉了。

sentences.en: I think you're attributing him with more power than he should have stepped in.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你赋予了他本不该由他介入的过大权力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So Heath wins that one.
sentences.zh: 所以希斯赢了那场大选。

sentences.en: And then people have listened to our 1974 series where we talk about the two elections of that year in which Heath manages to lose both of them.
sentences.zh: 然后大家听过我们1974年的系列节目，我们在节目里讨论了那一年的两次大选，在选举中希斯设法把两次都输掉了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He was a terrible performer, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 他的表现太糟糕了，不是吗？

sentences.en: And we had more liberal shenanigans with Jeremy Thorpe.
sentences.zh: 我们还有围绕杰里米·索普的更多自由党闹剧。

sentences.en: So 1974, I know we can't go into it because we did a whole series on that, but we have
sentences.zh: 所以1974年，我知道我们无法展开详谈，因为我们专门为此做过一整期节目，但我们有

sentences.en: Hovercraft, we have Jeremy Thorpe.
sentences.zh: 气垫船，我们有杰里米·索普。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: IRA bombs.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰共和军炸弹。

sentences.en: Enoch Powell.
sentences.zh: 伊诺克·鲍威尔。

sentences.en: If you listen to our series on 1974, which you can find on the rest is history, sort of page if you scroll down it, you will hear competing impersonations of Enoch Powell
sentences.zh: 如果你收听我们关于1974年的系列节目——你可以在《历史其余部分》的页面往下滚动找到它——你会听到对伊诺克·鲍威尔的各种模仿

sentences.en: and discussions of Howard Wilson's staff trying to murder his secretary.
sentences.zh: 以及关于哈罗德·威尔逊的工作人员试图谋杀其秘书的讨论。

sentences.en: So enjoy.
sentences.zh: 所以敬请欣赏。

sentences.en: So, you know, if 1970s elections are your thing, the 1974 series, you'll be absolutely in clover.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你对20世纪70年代的选举感兴趣，1974年的系列节目会让你如获至宝。

sentences.en: But just moving on to the election after that, 1979, which sees Mrs. Thatcher come to power and defeat James Callaghan.
sentences.zh: 但我们接着谈下一场选举，即1979年，撒切尔夫人正是在那次选举中上台并击败了詹姆斯·卡拉汉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There's a famous thing that James Callaghan is supposed to have said, and I'm sure you'll tell me he didn't say it, but Callaghan feels that the polls are against him, that
sentences.zh: 有个关于詹姆斯·卡拉汉的著名说法，我确信你会告诉我他根本没说过这话，但卡拉汉当时觉得民调对己方不利，

sentences.en: the Tories seem to be closing in.
sentences.zh: 保守党似乎正在步步紧逼。

sentences.en: And he's meant to have said to his aide, is it Bernard
sentences.zh: 据说他曾对他的助手说，是伯纳德

sentences.en: Donoghue?
sentences.zh: 多诺休吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And they're kind of driving around Parliament Square.
sentences.zh: 当时他们正开车绕着国会广场转。

sentences.en: And he says that there are times kind of like every 30 years when there is a sea change in politics and that this sea change is now working to the benefit of Mrs. Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 他说政治中每隔大约30年就会出现一次沧海桑田般的巨变，而这种巨变现在正朝着有利于撒切尔夫人的方向发展。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Do you think that's accurate?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这准确吗？

sentences.en: Do you think there are kind of rhythms in politics?
sentences.zh: 你觉得政治中存在某种韵律吗？

sentences.en: Because I know you're a great admirer of James Callaghan.
sentences.zh: 因为我知道你是詹姆斯·卡拉汉的超级崇拜者。

sentences.en: He has no greater admirer, Tom.
sentences.zh: 没人比他更崇拜卡拉汉了，汤姆。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I love this election because I actually like both party leaders.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这场选举，因为我实际上挺喜欢两党领袖的。

sentences.en: I can't lose.
sentences.zh: 我怎么都不会输。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: It's great.
sentences.zh: 这太好了。

sentences.en: So first of all, did he say that?
sentences.zh: 所以首先，他到底有没有说过这话？

sentences.en: And do you think that he's onto something when he says that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他说这话时是不是切中了要害？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, he's definitely onto something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，他确实切中了要害。

sentences.en: There are generational shifts.
sentences.zh: 存在着代际更迭。

sentences.en: I mean, we could talk about this in great detail.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们可以详细谈谈这个。

sentences.en: My friend Phil Tinline has written a book called
sentences.zh: 我的朋友菲尔·廷莱写过一本书叫

sentences.en: The Death of Consensus, which is all about this, which is all about how every 30 years or so there is a generational shift.
sentences.zh: 《共识之死》，整本书都在谈论这个，讲述了每隔30年左右就会发生一次代际更迭。

sentences.en: And there's a sense of the taboo shifting, the center ground shifting.
sentences.zh: 人们会有一种禁忌发生转移、中间立场发生转移的感觉。

sentences.en: The Overton window.
sentences.zh: 奥弗顿之窗。

sentences.en: The Overton window, as people call it.
sentences.zh: 正如人们所说的，奥弗顿之窗。

sentences.en: Exactly so.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: Callaghan did say something like it, but he didn't say what everyone thinks he said.
sentences.zh: 卡拉汉确实说过类似的话，但他说的并不是大家以为的那样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So here's the interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 所以有趣的地方就在这里。

sentences.en: And I think I'm the first person, the only person to have noticed this.
sentences.zh: 而且我想我是第一个、也是唯一一个注意到这一点的人。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So in Bernard Donoghue's memoir of that conversation, he absolutely says, Callaghan said to him, oh, we're not going to win.
sentences.zh: 所以在伯纳德·多诺休关于那次对话的回忆录里，他斩钉截铁地说，卡拉汉对他说，哦，我们赢不了了。

sentences.en: There's a sea change, Bernard, and you know, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 伯纳德，政治变天了，你知道的，巴拉巴拉。

sentences.en: Nothing you can say or do will make any difference.
sentences.zh: 你说什么或做什么都改变不了结局。

sentences.en: But actually, if you look at Bernard Donoghue's diary, which I did, which is also published, but nobody's bothered, as far as I'm aware, to compare the two.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如果你去看看伯纳德·多诺休的日记——我也这么做了，那也是公开出版的，但据我所知，没有人费心去把这两者做个对比。

sentences.en: He doesn't say that.
sentences.zh: 他根本没那样说。

sentences.en: In the diary, which was compiled closer to the time, Callaghan says, I'm actually feeling really good about the election.
sentences.zh: 在这本更接近当时记录的日记里，卡拉汉说，我其实对这次选举感觉非常好。

sentences.en: I think we actually might win this or do a lot better than people think, unless there has been a sea change.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们真的可能会赢，或者会比人们想象的要表现得好得多，除非政坛真的发生了巨变。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So in other words, Callaghan was feeling much more optimistic.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，卡拉汉当时的感觉要乐观得多。

sentences.en: There's a couple of interesting things here.
sentences.zh: 这里有几个有趣的点。

sentences.en: Number one is a lot of people say 79 is a great missed opportunity for Labour because Callaghan put that election off and had he held it earlier
sentences.zh: 第一点是，很多人说1979年对工党来说是一个极大的遗憾，因为卡拉汉推迟了那场选举，如果他早点举行大选，

sentences.en: before the great wave of strikes of the winter discontent, then he might have won and nobody would ever have heard of Margaret Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 在“不满的冬天”那波浩大的罢工潮之前举行，那么他可能就赢了，也就没人会知道玛格丽特·撒切尔是谁了。

sentences.en: Because he goes to the party conference the previous autumn, doesn't he, in 1978 and sings.
sentences.zh: 因为他在前一年秋天，也就是1978年，去参加了党代会，对吧，还在会上唱歌了。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他确实唱了。

sentences.en: Sings a song, There Was I Waiting at the Church.
sentences.zh: 唱了一首歌，名叫《当时我在教堂等待》。

sentences.en: It's actually the TUC conference, the trade unions.
sentences.zh: 那其实是工会大会，也就是工会联合会会议。

sentences.en: It's a musical song that no one knows what it means.
sentences.zh: 那是一首音乐剧歌曲，根本没人懂是什么意思。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: This is the age of the sex pistols.
sentences.zh: 这是性手枪乐队的时代。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He led everybody up the garden path thinking there'd be an election.
sentences.zh: 他把所有人都给耍了，让大家以为会有大选。

sentences.en: Then he put it off.
sentences.zh: 然后他又把选举推迟了。

sentences.en: I know why he put it off.
sentences.zh: 我知道他为什么推迟。

sentences.en: He put it off because all the data showed him that he wouldn't win it.
sentences.zh: 他推迟是因为所有数据都显示他赢不了。

sentences.en: Or at least if he did win it, it'd be so narrow that it would make his life a total misery.
sentences.zh: 或者至少，即使他赢了，优势也会极其微弱，那会让他的人生苦不堪言。

sentences.en: Gordon Brown did something similar, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 戈登·布朗也做过类似的事情，不是吗？

sentences.en: Which also was then a shadow over him because there was a feeling that he'd bottled it.
sentences.zh: 这也成了他挥之不去的阴影，因为人们觉得他是临阵退缩了。

sentences.en: I don't think Callaghan bottled it.
sentences.zh: 我不认为卡拉汉是临阵退缩。

sentences.en: I think he just made a call that, you know, we're probably not going to win the 78.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他只是做出了判断，你知道的，我们在78年可能赢不了。

sentences.en: We'll go for broken 79 and he loses anyway.
sentences.zh: 我们要在79年放手一搏，结果他还是输了。

sentences.en: Because there was a feeling, when was it?
sentences.zh: 因为当时有一种感觉，那是什么时候？

sentences.en: So I guess 2009.
sentences.zh: 我想大概是2009年吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That Gordon Brown had bottled it, that he'd planned to have an election and then didn't.
sentences.zh: 觉得戈登·布朗是临阵退缩了，他原本计划举行大选却没有举行。

sentences.en: Well, he'd planned to have an election in 2007, Tom, after he'd just come in.
sentences.zh: 哦，他是计划在2007年举行大选的，汤姆，就在他刚上任之后。

sentences.en: To have it before the financial crash.
sentences.zh: 打算在金融风暴爆发前举行。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I'm misremembering.
sentences.zh: 我记错了。

sentences.en: But by the time Callaghan does go to the country in 79, I think that election is a bit of a foregone conclusion.
sentences.zh: 但等到卡拉汉在1979年真正发起大选时，我觉得那场选举的结局已经毫无悬念了。

sentences.en: The winter discontent has happened.
sentences.zh: “不满的冬天”已经发生了。

sentences.en: There's a big shift to Thatcher among working class people, among young first-time voters.
sentences.zh: 工薪阶层和年轻的初次选民中出现了向撒切尔的大规模倒戈。

sentences.en: They break overwhelmingly for Thatcher in 79.
sentences.zh: 他们在1979年压倒性地投给了撒切尔。

sentences.en: There's a couple of really fun things about that election.
sentences.zh: 关于那场选举有几个非常有趣的地方。

sentences.en: So in the public imagination, this is the great ideological showdown between Labour and conservatism, between, you know, where Thatcherism arrives.
sentences.zh: 所以在公众的想象中，这是工党与保守党之间伟大的意识形态对决，也就是撒切尔主义登上历史舞台的时刻。

sentences.en: And some people, to be fair, at the time did say this.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，当时确实有些人这么说过。

sentences.en: So are you familiar with the satirist Orberon War?
sentences.zh: 所以你熟悉讽刺作家奥伯龙·沃吗？

sentences.en: I am.
sentences.zh: 我熟悉。

sentences.en: Evelyn War's son wrote a column in Private Eye.
sentences.zh: 伊夫林·沃的儿子，曾在《私家侦探》杂志写专栏。

sentences.en: He did.
sentences.zh: 他确实写过。

sentences.en: I think it was in that column or was it in The Spectator?
sentences.zh: 我想那是在他的专栏里，还是在《旁观者》杂志里？

sentences.en: I'm not sure which.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定是哪个。

sentences.en: This reads like it's from his column in Private Eye because, I mean, he was a very kind of reactionary, very crusty.
sentences.zh: 这段读起来就像他在《私家侦探》专栏里的风格，因为我的意思是，他非常反动，非常顽固。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, you know, he's the son of evil in war.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，你知道的，他是伊夫林·沃的儿子。

sentences.en: But in this column that he wrote for Private Eye, he would exaggerate that to kind of comically grotesque.
sentences.zh: 但在他为《私家侦探》写的这篇专栏里，他会把这种情绪夸大到一种滑稽而荒诞的程度。

sentences.zh: 达到一种庞大夸张的程度。

sentences.zh: 我想他在《名人录》里说过，他的爱好是说谎。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 所以他在文中说，这下迎来最终对决了。

sentences.zh: 他说，这是机会来了。

sentences.zh: 这是一场与对立阵营的战斗。

sentences.zh: 我引用一下，如果有什么人会被此冒犯，我向我们的听众道歉。

sentences.zh: 他确实这么做了。

sentences.en: He got on a soapbox.
sentences.zh: 他站上了肥皂箱。

sentences.en: And you were saying how politicians today haven't been seasoned in the school of hard knocks.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说现在的政客没有经历过残酷现实的历练。

sentences.en: They haven't been out on the streets.
sentences.zh: 他们没有去过基层街头。

sentences.en: But Major had.
sentences.zh: 但梅杰经历过。

sentences.en: Major was a councillor here in Brixton, where I'm sitting right now, and not a naturally Tory-friendly place, it has to be said.
sentences.zh: 梅杰曾是我现在正坐着的布里顿的一名议员，必须承认，这里并不是一个天然亲保守党的地方。

sentences.en: But he'd come through that, and he'd risen to become leader of the Tories.
sentences.zh: 但他历经磨炼，最终成为了保守党领袖。

sentences.en: And he thought, well, I'll go on the stump, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 他心想，好吧，我要去进行街头演说，对吧？

sentences.en: He got out his soapbox, and he took it round, and he had a loudspeaker, and people would gather and boo him and things.
sentences.zh: 他搬出他的肥皂箱，带着它四处奔走，拿着扩音器，人们会聚拢过来对发出嘘声之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, the soapbox is a wooden crate.
sentences.zh: 对，肥皂箱就是一个木箱子。

sentences.en: So basically, you put this crate down, and town centre, get up on the crate, get his loudspeaker, or loudhaler, and he'd say,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，你把这个箱子往市中心一放，站到箱子上去，拿着扩音器或高音喇叭，然后就会说，

sentences.en: you should vote Conservative because of blah, blah, blah, blah, in this sort of tinny, loud hailer voice.
sentences.zh: 你们应该投票给保守党，因为巴拉巴拉巴拉，用这种刺耳的、高音喇叭的声音。

sentences.en: And some people would say, rubbish, what about unemployment?
sentences.zh: 然后有些人就会说，胡扯，失业问题怎么说？

sentences.en: You know, whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，无所谓。

sentences.en: It was a great scene.
sentences.zh: 那是一个很棒的场面。

sentences.en: It was a throwback to an earlier age of politics.
sentences.zh: 那是对早期政治时代的一种复古致敬。

sentences.en: But it worked for him because he did have an unusual background for a Tory leader.
sentences.zh: 但这对很管用，因为他作为保守党领袖确实有着不寻常的背景。

sentences.en: The circus.
sentences.zh: 马戏团。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's famously the only man to have run away from the circus to join an accountancy firm.
sentences.zh: 对，他最出名的就是唯一一个从马戏团逃跑去加入会计事务所的人。

sentences.en: But he actually, they did a party political broadcast in that campaign where he went back to Brixton, and he kind of revisited all his old haunts.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他们在当年的那场竞选中做过一次政党政治广播，他回到了布里克斯顿，重访了他所有老地方。

sentences.en: It's actually really well done.
sentences.zh: 其实真的做得很好。

sentences.en: Because he's in the car.
sentences.zh: 因为他坐在车里。

sentences.en: The car is going towards his old house.
sentences.zh: 车子正驶向他以前的房子。

sentences.en: He's saying, is it there?
sentences.zh: 他说，还在吗？

sentences.en: Is it there?
sentences.zh: 还在吗？

sentences.en: It's still there.
sentences.zh: 还在。

sentences.en: Look, it's still there.
sentences.zh: 看，还在。

sentences.en: He's talking about his old house.
sentences.zh: 他说的是他以前的房子。

sentences.en: And this sort of thing that he is, he is so ordinary, and the ordinariness is the point.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉就是，他太普通了，而这种普通就是关键所在。

sentences.en: Well, you say that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你这么说。

sentences.en: I mean, I agree.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我同意。

sentences.en: The ordinariness was the point, and was his kind of USP, really.
sentences.zh: 普通就是关键，说实话这也是他的一种独特卖点。

sentences.en: But the weird thing is, on television, he did come across very boring, and he's always portrayed as very grey and eating peas and, you know, tucking his shirt into his pants.
sentences.zh: 但奇怪的是，在电视上，他给人的感觉真的很无聊，而且总是被描绘成非常古板、吃豌豆，你知道的，把衬衫扎进裤子里。

sentences.en: But I've met him a couple of times in person.
sentences.zh: 但我私下里见过他几次。

sentences.en: He's a very charismatic man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常有个人魅力的人。

sentences.en: I mean, he's very kind of tall, good looking, amusing, funny.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他个子很高，长相帅气，很逗趣，很滑稽。

sentences.en: And I just wonder whether going out into the streets enabled that aspect of him.
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，走上街头是不是更能展现他这一面。

sentences.en: There was something about television that kind of bleached him of what made him an impressive figure in person.
sentences.zh: 电视似乎有某种魔力，把他在现实中那种令人印象深刻的特质给过滤掉了。

sentences.en: I agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我同意这一点。

sentences.en: And Tom, I don't think we should turn this into the John Major fan caSt. But all of that said, I once went to an event
sentences.zh: 还有汤姆，我觉得我们不应该把这变成约翰·梅杰的粉丝俱乐部。但话虽如此，我曾经去参加过一个活动

sentences.en: at the National Archives, in my capacities, on the board of their trust, whatever.
sentences.zh: 在国家档案馆，以我作为他们信托基金会董事的身份，诸如此类的。

sentences.en: And
sentences.zh: 然后

sentences.en: John Major came to give a speech about archives.
sentences.zh: 约翰·梅杰来做一个关于档案馆的演讲。

sentences.en: And I thought, this is going to be the worst thing ever.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，这绝对是有史以来最糟糕的事情了。

sentences.en: A speech about archives, which is intrinsically quite boring, and I say that as a historian.
sentences.zh: 一个关于档案馆的演讲，这本身就很无聊，作为一个历史学家我得这么说。

sentences.en: And B, it's by John Major.
sentences.zh: 第二，这是约翰·梅杰讲的。

sentences.en: And he stood up, and he gave his speech, and I thought, Jesus Christ, he's good.
sentences.zh: 然后他站起来，做了一个演讲，当时我想，天哪，他太厉害了。

sentences.en: That was one of the best speeches I've ever heard.
sentences.zh: 那是我听过的最好的演讲之一。

sentences.en: And then he went around shaking people's hands and introducing.
sentences.zh: 接着他走过去跟人们握手并做自我介绍。

sentences.en: He's very tall, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他个子很高，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He's like, formidably physical.
sentences.zh: 他有一种极具压迫感的体魄。

sentences.en: I say it's charismatic, is the word.
sentences.zh: 我说得有魅力，就是这个词。

sentences.en: I know it sounds absolutely bonkers to say that of John Major.
sentences.zh: 我知道对约翰·梅杰用这个词听起来绝对疯狂。

sentences.en: I thought, I mean, that election, both leaders were very charismatic.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，那次选举中，两位领袖都极具个人魅力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And if you think about the people we've had in more recent elections, that sense of charisma and moral power combined, both of them had it in their different ways.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想我们近几次选举中遇到的人，那种魅力与道德力量的结合，他们两人以各自不同的方式都具备。

sentences.en: Kinnock.
sentences.zh: 金诺克。

sentences.en: So I've interviewed Kinnock and spent time with him.
sentences.zh: 所以我采访过金诺克，也和他相处过。

sentences.en: He's an incredibly charismatic man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个极具个人魅力的人。

sentences.en: He's a great fan to be around.
sentences.zh: 和他在一起是一件很棒的事。

sentences.en: A joker, good-humoured, again, a real presence to him.
sentences.zh: 是个开心果，幽默风趣，同样，有着真正的气场。

sentences.en: Goodness, could he articulate his ideals in a way that kind of made the hair on the back of your neck rise?
sentences.zh: 天哪，他阐述理想的方式怎么能让你起一身鸡皮疙瘩呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely agreed.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: I remember that election campaign.
sentences.zh: 我还记得那场选举竞选。

sentences.en: It was the first time I was in London.
sentences.zh: 那是我第一次去伦敦。

sentences.en: I found it exciting.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得很兴奋。

sentences.en: And, you know, you didn't quite know who was going to win.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，你不太确定谁会赢。

sentences.en: And I thought both the leaders were very impressive.
sentences.zh: 我觉得两位领导人都非常令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: As, actually, the Labour leader who campaigns in the next election in 1997, also, I thought.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在下一次1997年的大选中参加竞选的工党领袖也是如此，我觉得。

sentences.en: Well, Tom, let me read you this and you tell me which election you think this is from.
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，让我给你读一段，你来猜猜这是哪次选举。

sentences.en: It's from American Coverage.
sentences.zh: 这是来自美国媒体的报道。

sentences.en: From Oxford's genteel debating scientists to tattooed punk rockers, Britain's youth seems to speak with the same voice about the May the 1st election.
sentences.zh: 从牛津温文尔雅的辩论学者到文身朋克摇滚乐手，英国青年似乎用同一种声音在谈论5月1日的选举。

sentences.en: And that voice seems to be saying, who cares?
sentences.zh: 而那个声音似乎在说，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: I don't think whatever happens is going to make any difference.
sentences.zh: 我觉得无论发生什么都不会有任何改变。

sentences.en: See, it's 1945 again, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你看，这又是1945年了，汤姆。

sentences.en: I don't think whatever happens is going to make any difference, said a young woman in a jean jacket, a pair of fashionable sunglasses perched on her head.
sentences.zh: 一个穿着牛仔夹克、头上架着一副时髦太阳镜的年轻女子说，我觉得无论发生什么都不会有任何改变。

sentences.en: But will she vote?
sentences.zh: 但她会投票吗？

sentences.en: Never have done, never will do, she chirped.
sentences.zh: 从来没投过，以后也绝不会投，她轻快地说。

sentences.en: And her friend added simultaneously, no, sorry, I would vote if I knew more about it, said a dark haired woman in carefully applied makeup.
sentences.zh: 她的朋友同时补充道，不，抱歉，如果我对它了解更多的话我会投票的，一个画着精致妆容的黑发女子说。

sentences.en: I would, but I don't.
sentences.zh: 我会投的，但我并不了解。

sentences.en: So I'm not going to vote.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会去投票。

sentences.en: Now, which election is that?
sentences.zh: 那么，那是哪场选举？

sentences.en: That's 97, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我猜是97年。

sentences.en: So the supposed, everybody's very enthusiastic, things can only get better,
sentences.zh: 所以大家本以为所有人都会非常热情，情况只会越来越好，

sentences.en: Blair landslide, cool Britannia.
sentences.zh: 布莱尔压倒性胜选，酷不列颠。

sentences.en: And yet the interesting thing about that, Tony Blair did not enthuse people, as everybody says.
sentences.zh: 然而有趣的是，托尼·布莱尔并没有像每个人说的那样激起人们的热情。

sentences.en: Now, if you listen to Alistair Campbell on The Rest is Politics, I'm sure he'll tell you something different.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你听听《政治其余部分》节目里的阿拉斯泰尔·坎贝尔，我确信他会告诉你一些不同的东西。

sentences.en: Don't it, you're wrong.
sentences.zh: 难道不是吗，你错了。

sentences.en: He absolutely enthused me.
sentences.zh: 他绝对激起了我的热情。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但问题是。

sentences.en: Turnout was fully 6% lower in 1997 than 1992.
sentences.zh: 1997年的投票率比1992年足足低了6%。

sentences.en: But that's because everyone knew Labour were going to win.
sentences.zh: 但那是因为大家都知道工党会赢。

sentences.en: People turn out when it's unclear who's going to win, surely.
sentences.zh: 只有在谁赢谁输还不确定的时候，人们才会出来投票，肯定的。

sentences.en: The Blair effect is not to fire people up with political enthusiasm, it's just to turn them off politics.
sentences.zh: 布莱尔效应并不是用政治热情点燃人们，而是让他们对政治倒胃口。

sentences.en: Because, Dominic, totally wrong.
sentences.zh: 因为，多米尼克，大错特错。

sentences.en: Let me continue.
sentences.zh: 让我继续。

sentences.en: I've got the facts, and you don't.
sentences.zh: 我有事实，而你没有。

sentences.en: I've got anecdotal evidence, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 我有轶事证据，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Rubbish.
sentences.zh: 胡说。

sentences.en: In 2001, turnout fell even lower under Blair, to 59%, its lowest level since 1918.
sentences.zh: 在2001年，在布莱尔的领导下，投票率进一步下降至59%，创下1918年以来的最低水平。

sentences.en: So actually, Blair works as the ultimate political turnoff.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，布莱尔起到了终极政治劝退的作用。

sentences.en: The more people see of him, the less likely they are to vote on either side.
sentences.zh: 人们见到他的次数越多，他们在两边投票的可能性就越小。

sentences.en: But the reason for that, surely, is that people just assume he's going to win.
sentences.zh: 但原因肯定是因为人们默认他会赢。

sentences.en: Well, we'll see this time, won't we?
sentences.zh: 好吧，这次我们拭目以待，不是吗？

sentences.en: Whether that is the same.
sentences.zh: 看看是不是还一样。

sentences.en: I mean, everybody thought Boris was going to win in 2019, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大家都以为鲍里斯会在2019年赢，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, ultimately, you can't deny that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，归根结底，你不能否认这一点。

sentences.en: Everyone thought Boris Johnson was going to win.
sentences.zh: 每个人都以为鲍里斯·约翰逊会赢。

sentences.en: And turnout then was almost 10% higher in 2019 than it was in 1997.
sentences.zh: 而2019年的投票率比1997年高了将近10%。

sentences.en: But 2019, there was lots at stake.
sentences.zh: 但2019年有很多利益攸关的事情。

sentences.en: And there wasn't in 97?
sentences.zh: 97年就没有吗？

sentences.en: People just thought, oh, we're fed up.
sentences.zh: 人们只是觉得，哦，我们受够了。

sentences.en: Tory's been around forever.
sentences.zh: 保守党在台下待了太久了。

sentences.en: Things are going to get better.
sentences.zh: 情况会好起来的。

sentences.en: I know Goldhanger podcast is like a Tony Blair fan zone, and they don't want to hear it.
sentences.zh: 我知道戈德亨格播客就像一个托尼·布莱尔粉丝专区，他们不想听这些。

sentences.en: Listen, Dominic, you have your stats and your figures, but I have my anecdotal evidence and my memories.
sentences.zh: 听着，多米尼克，你有你的统计数据和数字，但我有我的轶事证据和回忆。

sentences.en: So what's your favourite?
sentences.zh: 所以你最喜欢哪一次？

sentences.en: There's been four elections since 2010.
sentences.zh: 自2010年以来已经举行过四次选举了。

sentences.en: So there's 2010, Cameron and Clegg hung parliament.
sentences.zh: 所以有2010年，卡梅伦和克莱格的悬峙议会。

sentences.en: 2015, Miliband.
sentences.zh: 2015年，米利班德。

sentences.en: I did quite enjoy that.
sentences.zh: 我其实挺享受那次选举的。

sentences.en: Labour were terrible in that election.
sentences.zh: 工党在那次选举中表现得太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And it was full of comic moments.
sentences.zh: 而且充满了滑稽的时刻。

sentences.en: My favourite bit was when Ed Miliband went to see Russell Brand, the comedian and person who's been accused of all kinds of bad behaviour.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的部分是埃德·米利班德去见喜剧演员拉塞尔·布兰德，也就是那个被指控有各种不良行为的人。

sentences.en: Controversial star.
sentences.zh: 充满争议的明星。

sentences.en: And your old student, Owen Jones, wrote an article about it saying,
sentences.zh: 而你的老学生欧文·琼斯写了一篇文章说，

sentences.en: Russell Brand has come out for Labour and the Tories should be worried.
sentences.zh: 拉塞尔·布兰德已经公开支持工党，保守党该担心了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember that.
sentences.zh: 对，我记得那个。

sentences.en: I still think that's the funniest headline about a general election campaign that I can think of.
sentences.zh: 我仍然认为这是我能想到的关于大选竞选的最搞笑的标题。

sentences.en: And it's obviously, in light of recent events, it's become even funnier.
sentences.zh: 鉴于最近发生的事件，这显然变得更加滑稽了。

sentences.en: As the Tories eased to that overall majority.
sentences.zh: 随着保守党轻松赢得绝对多数。

sentences.en: So then there's 2017.
sentences.zh: 接下来是2017年。

sentences.en: Now, 2017 is another one that basically punctures my thesis, because 2017, the campaign did matter.
sentences.zh: 现在，2017年是另一个基本上推翻了我的论点的案例，因为在2017年，竞选确实很重要。

sentences.en: Because if the election had been held and there'd be no campaign, I think Theresa May would have won a handsome, handsome majority.
sentences.zh: 因为如果选举举行而没有竞选过程的话，我认为特雷莎·梅会赢得一个非常可观的多数优势。

sentences.en: But unfortunately, she insisted on campaigning.
sentences.zh: 但不幸的是，她坚持要进行竞选。

sentences.en: And she was just such a stilted and just not a natural campaigner.
sentences.zh: 而她偏偏是那种显得很不自然、根本不是个天生政治竞选人的人。

sentences.en: I mean, weirdly, for someone who got to the top of politics, she's not a huckster, not a salesman.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，奇怪的是，对于一个登上政治巅峰的人来说，她不是个政客腔调的人，也不是个推销员。

sentences.en: And of course, Jeremy Corbyn was not really saying anything very substantive, I wouldn't say.
sentences.zh: 当然，杰里米·科尔宾也没有说任何实质性的东西，我觉得。

sentences.en: I mean, I think they were both absolutely terrible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为他们俩都太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And if you compare Major and Kinnett or Callaghan and Thatcher, you just kind of weep.
sentences.zh: 如果你把梅杰和金诺克，或者卡拉汉和撒切尔进行比较，你简直会有一种想哭的冲动。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I know that there's always the risk, it's a bit like music or sport, that people who kind of live in your memory when you first get into something,
sentences.zh: 我知道这总是存在风险，这有点像音乐或体育，那些在你刚开始接触某事时留在你记忆中的人，

sentences.en: or you first become aware of something, always seem more vivid.
sentences.zh: 或者当你刚开始了解某事时，总是显得更为生动。

sentences.en: So there's always the risk, you know, I'm now in my 50s, that the political leaders of my youth seem more impressive.
sentences.zh: 所以总会有这样的风险，你知道的，我现在50多岁了，我年轻时的政治领袖似乎显得更加令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: I don't think it is, though.
sentences.zh: 不过我不认为这是错觉。

sentences.en: I genuinely think that the leaders in the 80s and 90s were qualitatively better, both as campaigners and as leaders, than they have been recently.
sentences.zh: 我真心认为80年代和90年代的领袖，无论作为竞选人还是作为领袖，在质量上都比近年来的要好。

sentences.en: But let's end by just discussing this point, has the standard declined in this period we've been talking about?
sentences.zh: 但让我们以讨论这个问题来结束吧，在我们一直在讨论的这段时期里，水准下降了吗？

sentences.en: We started in 1945, right, Churchill and Attlee.
sentences.zh: 我们从1945年开始，对吧，丘吉尔和艾德礼。

sentences.en: When Churchill entered the House of Commons in the 1900s, he said of that House of Commons, there were still big personalities in it,
sentences.zh: 当丘吉尔在20世纪初进入下议院时，他对那个下议院说，里面仍然有很多个性鲜明的大人物，

sentences.en: though of course it had declined since my father's day.
sentences.zh: 尽管与我父亲的时代相比，它确实已经走下坡路了。

sentences.en: And you look at that House of Commons, right, which has Churchill, it will go on to have like Keir Hardee, Attlee, all these great figures in the Labour Party.
sentences.zh: 你看看那个下议院，对吧，里面有丘吉尔，后来还会有基尔·哈迪、艾德礼，工党的这些伟大人物。

sentences.en: If I ask with Lloyd George, Richard Haldane, Joseph Chamberlain, you're like, what?
sentences.zh: 如果我问到劳埃德·乔治、理查德·霍尔丹、约瑟夫·张伯伦，你就会想，什么？

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我懂的。

sentences.en: And I'm aware that people are always thinking that politics is in decline.
sentences.zh: 我也知道人们总觉得政治在走下坡路。

sentences.en: But I've reached that stage where I genuinely think it is.
sentences.zh: 但我已经到了那个阶段，我由衷地觉得确实如此。

sentences.en: So I can't help it.
sentences.zh: 所以我无能为力。

sentences.en: I'm middle-aged.
sentences.zh: 我已经中年了。

sentences.en: Who cares?
sentences.zh: 谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: But just because people always say it doesn't mean it can't be true.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅因为人们总是这么说，并不意味着它就不是真的。

sentences.en: And I think there is no doubt that the standard of the personnel and of the campaigns, and in other words, generally the context, the ecosystem, has changed and not for the better.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为毫无疑问，人员的水准和竞选的水准，换句话说，总体上的环境、生态系统，已经发生了变化，而且是在向不好的方向变化。

sentences.en: And why do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: So I think there's a couple of reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得有几个原因。

sentences.en: To be brutal, politicians pay much less than they were relative to other professions.
sentences.zh: 说句戳心的话，与其他行业相比，政客的薪酬比以前低多了。

sentences.en: So in other words, if you're a very ambitious, talented person, you may be inhibited from going into politics.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你是一个雄心勃勃、才华横溢的人，你可能会对从政望而却步。

sentences.en: The demands are much greater.
sentences.zh: 要求高得多。

sentences.en: It's a very peculiar lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常奇特的生活方式。

sentences.en: I think a lot of it is actually, we talked about how there'd been a transition from the mass rallies to the televised campaigns and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我想很大程度上是因为，我们之前讨论过从群众集会向电视竞选等形式的转变。

sentences.en: And I think the ecosystem, the context, the environment makes it almost impossible for politicians to shine because they are interviewed on the BBC's, frankly,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这种生态、背景和环境使得政客几乎不可能大放异彩，因为他们在BBC的节目里接受采访，说实话，

sentences.en: terrible political shows for, what, three minutes?
sentences.zh: 那些糟糕的政治节目，大概只有三分钟？

sentences.en: They're given three answers.
sentences.zh: 他们只回答三个问题。

sentences.en: And if they say the slightest slip, people seize on it.
sentences.zh: 如果他们有丝毫口误，人们就会抓住不放。

sentences.en: I mean, here's a really good example.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这里有个很好的例子。

sentences.en: Churchill would be interviewed, or Wilson or whoever,
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔会接受采访，或者威尔逊或其他人，

sentences.en: and they would give a long answer that would go on for five minutes and they'd say all kinds of different things and no one would really notice.
sentences.zh: 他们会给出长达五分钟的冗长回答，谈论各种各样不同的事情，而没有人会真正注意到。

sentences.en: Rishi Sunak appears on the radio.
sentences.zh: 里希·苏纳克出现在电台节目中。

sentences.en: He makes a joke about how he's been eating Haribos and Twix's, like sweets, to keep himself going in the campaign.
sentences.zh: 他开玩笑说自己一直在吃哈瑞宝和特克斯糖果之类的零食，来支撑自己完成竞选。

sentences.en: It's just an offhand joke.
sentences.zh: 这只是一句随口的玩笑。

sentences.en: And immediately someone rings up the station to complain and says, how cruel and insensitive that at a time when we're battling with obesity,
sentences.zh: 立刻就有人打电话到电台投诉，说在我们要与肥胖作斗争的时期，这样做是多么残忍和麻木不仁，

sentences.en: it says so much about the prime minister that he would make an offhand remark about eating sweets in this way.
sentences.zh: 这充分说明了这位首相竟然会随口说出吃糖果这样的话。

sentences.en: But doesn't that just reflect the fact that social media now means that people can be incredibly humorless in a loud way about everything that a politician says?
sentences.zh: 但这不恰恰反映出社交媒体现在意味着人们可以对政客说的每一句话进行大张旗鼓、毫无幽默感的批判吗？

sentences.en: It does, of course, but it basically means politicians, their room to breathe has been so restricted.
sentences.zh: 当然是的，但这基本上意味着政客们的生存空间被极大地压缩了。

sentences.en: So there was an age when maybe Sunak Starmer, when they could actually have grown as politicians and as people, we could have seen a reflective side.
sentences.zh: 所以曾经有过这样一个时代，也许像苏纳克和斯塔默，他们当时可以真正作为政客和个人成长，我们本可以看到他们沉稳的一面。

sentences.en: They must have reflective sides.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定有沉稳的一面。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't believe they're stupid people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不相信他们是蠢人。

sentences.en: Well, I actually think that both of them, relative to the leaders that we had in more recent times, are much more impressive.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我实际上认为他们两个与我们近年来遇到的领导人相比，要深刻得多。

sentences.en: I could imagine them appearing in a 1979 political broadcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象他们出现在1979年的政治广播中。

sentences.en: Well, here's the thing, if you had to put your family finances in the hands of Jeremy Corbyn, Boris Johnson, Keir Starmer, Rishi Sunak, all his truSt.
sentences.zh: 好吧，问题是，如果你必须把家庭财务交托给杰里米·科尔宾、鲍里斯·约翰逊、基尔·斯塔默、里希·苏纳克，所有的信任。

sentences.en: I mean, there's two people there who are in a different league from all the others, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，那里有两个人和其他所有人不在一个量级上，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 对，我也这么觉得。

sentences.en: So I think that's quite a positive notion on which to end.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这是一个相当积极的结束语。

sentences.en: That's quintessential centrist addery, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 典型的中间派老调重弹，对吧？

sentences.en: No, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 不，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我不这么觉得。

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我觉得就是。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: I think there'll be some people listening to this and saying, what absolute melts, Corbyn is the man.
sentences.zh: 我想有些人听了这话会觉得，真是两个十足的软蛋，科尔宾才是不二人选。

sentences.en: Or there'll be people who say, slagging off Boris again, that's such rest is politics behaviour.
sentences.zh: 或者有人会说，又在讽刺鲍里斯了，这太符合《政治播客》的风格了。

sentences.en: No, because I think that Mrs. Thatcher was a very, very impressive campaigner.
sentences.zh: 不，因为我认为撒切尔夫人是一位非常、非常出色的竞选者。

sentences.en: I think Attlee was.
sentences.zh: 我觉得艾德礼也是。

sentences.en: Oh, Attlee's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 哦，艾德礼太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, there are people who have led radical, transformative governments.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有些人领导过激进且具有变革性的政府。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Who are clearly very impressive in all kinds of ways.
sentences.zh: 他们在各方面显然都非常优秀。

sentences.en: I know who you're ultimately talking about, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我知道你最终说的是谁。

sentences.en: You're talking about H.H.
sentences.zh: 你说的是H·H·阿斯奎斯，对吧？

sentences.en: Asquith, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So he will be joining us for the First World War.
sentences.zh: 所以他将和我们一起探讨第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: Over the next few weeks.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几周里。

sentences.en: So we are about to embark on an epic account of the build-up to the First World War.
sentences.zh: 所以我们即将开始一段史诗般的叙述，讲述一战前的风雨欲来。

sentences.en: So next week, we start a four-part series on the murder of the Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo.
sentences.zh: 所以下周，我们将开始一个四部分的系列节目，讲述萨拉热窝刺杀奥匈帝国皇储弗朗茨·斐迪南大公的事件。

sentences.en: Four episodes on that.
sentences.zh: 共四集内容。

sentences.en: And then we have a kind of sister series, six parts, looking at the road from Sarajevo to Britain's entry into the war on the 4th of AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 然后我们有一个类似姐妹篇的六集系列，探讨从萨拉热窝到8月4日英国参战的道路。

sentences.en: And I hope you enjoy that.
sentences.zh: 希望你们会喜欢。

sentences.en: Well, Tom, they can't not enjoy it because it involves the best impressions you've ever done.
sentences.zh: 好吧，汤姆，他们不可能不喜欢，因为这包含了你做过最棒的模仿秀。

sentences.en: I think you doing the Kaiser will live in my memory till my dying day.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你模仿德皇的表演让我至死难忘。

sentences.en: And people say that, you know, you do impersonations and the impersonations takes you over.
sentences.zh: 人们都说，你知道的，你做模仿，然后模仿反过来主导了你。

sentences.en: One of the really startling things, I think, about the series on the build-up to the war is the fact that over the course of it, I discover that I am actually the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 关于一战前夕这个系列节目，最令人震惊的一点是，在节目的录制过程中，我发现我其实就是德皇本人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The similarities are uncanny.
sentences.zh: 相似之处惊人地一致。

sentences.en: Uncanny.
sentences.zh: 惊人。

sentences.en: Came as a surprise.
sentences.zh: 这确实是个惊喜。

sentences.en: But the more I contemplated it, the more I came to accept its force.
sentences.zh: 但我想得越多，就越发接受了这个事实。

sentences.en: I think we discovered, didn't we, that basically we've often talked about what the dynamic is at the heart of this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我想我们发现了，对吧？我们经常讨论这个播客的核心动力是什么。

sentences.en: And it actually is the relationship between Franz Ferdinand and the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 而实际上它就是弗朗茨·斐迪南和德皇之间的关系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We love a hunting lodge.
sentences.zh: 我们太喜欢狩猎小屋了。

sentences.en: Let's be frank.
sentences.zh: 坦白说。

sentences.en: So lots to look forward to, I hope.
sentences.zh: 所以希望有很多内容值得期待。

sentences.en: And for our British listeners, enjoy the last week of the election campaign.
sentences.zh: 对于我们的英国听众，祝你们享受大选的最后一周。

sentences.en: If you can.
sentences.zh: 如果你们还受得了的话。

sentences.en: If you can.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话。

sentences.en: And we hope you enjoy the brutal murder in Sarajevo of the Archduke Franz Ferdinand.
sentences.zh: 我们也希望你们能喜欢萨拉热窝弗朗茨·斐迪南大公被残忍谋杀的桥段。

sentences.en: So until then, bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 那么在此之前，再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
